items.title: Les Gets World Cup Breakdown | €100K Won & A French Fairytale
items.description:
Hattie Harnden just won the €100,000 Gates Belted Purse, Max Alran took his first Elite World Cup victory in front of an incredible home crowd, and Les Gets delivered another absolutely wild weekend of downhill racing.

After a six-week break, Chris is joined by Olly Morris and Neko Mulally to break down everything that happened at the Les Gets UCI Downhill World Cup.

At the centre of the women's race was Hattie Harnden. In constantly changing conditions, Hattie found the speed and lines she needed to take her first Elite Downhill World Cup victory and, with it, finally secure the €100,000 Gates Belted Purse for AON Racing.

It's also a significant moment technically. Hattie's AON bike uses a belt-driven gearbox drivetrain and a radically different approach to weight distribution and setup. Winning at Les Gets proves that concept can deliver at the very highest level of World Cup downhill racing.

We dig into Hattie's run, the crucial line choices that made the difference and what the result means for AON, before looking across a stacked women's race that also saw Vali Höll secure the 2026 World Cup overall with two rounds still remaining.

Then there's Max Alran.

Fastest in timed training, winner of Q1 and last man down the mountain at his home World Cup, Max delivered when it mattered. He crossed the line 1.650 seconds ahead of Andreas Kolb to claim his first Elite World Cup victory as the Les Gets hillside erupted around him.

We break down Max's incredible weekend alongside Andreas Kolb, Jackson Goldstone, Richie Rude, Antoine Pierron, Amaury Pierron, Jordan Williams and the developing men's overall battle.

There's plenty more too, including the extraordinary weather that transformed the track, brutal qualifying conditions, tyre and setup decisions, practice limitations, the rapidly changing lines riders faced during finals and standout performances across the Junior fields.

From Hattie's €100k breakthrough and Max's home victory to Vali wrapping up the overall, this was another reminder of why Les Gets continues to produce some of the most memorable racing on the World Cup calendar.

Next stop: the 2026 UCI Mountain Bike World Championships in Val di Sole.

items.title: Qualifying Madness in Les Gets with Asa Vermette and Gracey Hemstreet - The Setup | FOX
items.description:
After a few weeks away following Andorra, the circus rolls into Les Gets, where a passionate home crowd will be out in force to back the French riders.
 
But this weekend could be about more than home advantage. With a questionable forecast on the horizon, conditions could get rough, unpredictable, and seriously muddy. If the weather turns, expect sliding rear wheels, sketchy lines and plenty of surprises as riders battle their way down the track.
 
In this episode of The Set Up, we look ahead to what’s coming in Les Gets, the home crowd advantage, the French charge, and how the weather could shake up the form book for Round 7. Asa Vermette remains in the conversation for the overall, while Gracey Hemstreet won here last year in similar conditions. We’re excited to see how things unfold on race day and who’s done their homework over the summer break.
 
Welcome to Les Gets. Welcome to The Set Up.

items.title: The Fight | THE GRIND - Episode 2 | A Monster Energy Documentary Series
items.description:
Nine rounds. Three riders. One season.

The races keep coming, the fatigue is growing, and the pressure is always there.

Follow Luca Martin, Gwendalyn Gibson and Charlie Aldridge through the next chapter of the 2026 UCI Cross-Country World Cup season, as they take on Lenzerheide, La Thuile and Pal Arinsal.

At this stage of the season, the roles are beginning to take shape. Luca is fighting to defend the overall lead after an incredible run of results. Charlie is fighting his way back to his best after a difficult start to the season. Gwendalyn continues to deliver consistent results while facing the growing physical demands of the UCI World Cup circuit.

From intense battles on the course to crashes, recovery, team briefings and the moments between races, Episode 2 goes beyond the results to explore what it takes to keep pushing when the season starts to take its toll.

Three riders. Three different battles. One season that is only getting harder.

More than a race recap, The Grind explores the people behind the results, revealing the pressure, the fatigue, the setbacks, the rivalries and the reality of life on the UCI Cross-Country World Cup circuit.

The season is getting harder. The fight is just beginning.
